The top comment has input lag for TV's of 2015. The lowest input lag for the TV's tested is 19ms, upwards to 79ms. That is going to make a difference in any FPS. Low end monitors have input lag around 7ms and can drop to 1ms can buy a 2ms 1080p IPS for 150. Definitely a big difference for any online multiplayer.

I don't think you'd even be able to tell the difference. You see a wide gap between numbers but do not seem to grasp how minuscule the scale really is. Really think about how long 1 millisecond is (0.001 seconds) compared to even 60 milliseconds (0.060 seconds).
If you're playing online games, you already have to deal with around 40-80ms of ping latency. A high input lag TV could easily double that latency.

lolwut? No.

You see these events as a linear thing, but they don't run linearly. They run in parallel. You don't add your display latency to your network latency to come up with your total latency because that's not how it works. Your console is going to send out a network update as soon as it can and that will nearly always run in a separate thread. Your television has no impact on that whatsoever. Even if you were to turn your TV off (which would reduce its latency to 0) it's not like network updates would suddenly occur faster or slower.

The TV does not affect the network latency, but it does affect the net latency to perceive it.

Say you have 80ms ping, and a TV with 80ms latency. On a server somewhere, an enemy player steps in from of your player. This information then takes 40ms to travel from the server to your PC. When the information gets the the PC, the player still does not know, because it will take another 80 ms to get from the PC to the TV. Then, once the player sees it and reacts, it will take another 40ms for the PC to send a command to the server. Total time elapsed is 160 ms. Not because the TV affects the PC's network latency, but because it affects the time it takes to get information to the player.

Many modern TVs have an input lag of over 150ms outside "gaming mode" and a barely acceptable 50ms or so with "gaming mode" turned on. If you're an avid gamer, you'll notice this as soon as you move your mouse/controller.

Also, since the question was asked about PC gaming, one would assume that the user is playing at at least 60fps without much other input lag - even a 25ms lag would become quite noticeable to an experienced gamer. Please don't patronize 2016 PC gamers about 1080p either, we've been doing "4k" or higher for decades now.
